A deaf Dogo Argentino who was surrendered to a shelter as a puppy is now geared up in military fatigues and preparing to deploy with the Michigan National Guard’s 1st Battalion, 125th Infantry Regiment.

Actual Article Body:
A deaf Dogo Argentino who was surrendered to a shelter as a puppy is now geared up in military fatigues and preparing to deploy with the Michigan National Guard’s 1st Battalion, 125th Infantry Regiment.

Three-year-old Axel serves as the battalion’s official ministry dog alongside his handler, Sergeant Mollie Karazim, a religious affairs specialist. Unable to hear standard verbal commands, Axel was trained with a custom system of visual cues, hand signals, and American Sign Language (ASL), mastering over 50 individual commands.

WASHINGTON — Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi insisted that his country is fully prepared for a “doomsday war” with the US, but claimed the regime prefers peace.

“We stand firm in the face of any aggression against us, even when it comes to a doomsday war,” Araghchi told NBC’s “Meet the Press” on Sunday. “At the same time, we are ready for diplomacy.”

Araghchi pointed to Iran’s seven-day cease-fire proposal as a “very reasonable plan on the table,” despite President Trump’s decision to reject that overture.
